reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must accept SEARCH identifier-1 [VARYING {identifier-2 | index-name-1}] [AT END imp-1] {WHEN condition-1 {imp-2 | NEXT SENTENCE}}... [END-SEARCH] and SEARCH ALL identifier-1 [AT END imp-1] WHEN {data-name-1 {IS EQUAL TO | IS =} {identifier-3 | literal-1 | arithmetic-expression-1} | condition-name-1} [AND ...]... {imp-2 | NEXT SENTENCE} [END-SEARCH] (the whole statement boxed level 2), and refuse shapes neither format prints; the witnesses cover NEXT SENTENCE bodies only.

reader.notes: The grammar spells both formats; Format 2's single WHEN and its EQUAL-only AND chain are narrowed by the grammar and SearchAllFormat2Rules with named diagnostics. The level-2 box covers the whole statement, a level marker rather than an edition arm; the compiler implements the full level and has no subset mode. Two refusals (no WHEN, NOT AT END) carry a generic COBOL0001.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/md85-coderead/probes-refute/src. Class b: RS01 SEARCH ALL E WHEN 03 = K1 (IX) (key on the right) -> COBOL1965/1966 (§1985:VI.6.22.3 SR4); RS03B Format 1 AT END after WHEN -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'AT'; RS04 WHEN NOT condition-name -> COBOL1757 'this WHEN specifies a NOT'; RS05 parenthesized Format-2 condition -> COBOL1757; RS06 VARYING 5 -> COBOL5506 no literal expected; RS08 WHEN body ADD ... ON SIZE ERROR without END-ADD -> COBOL2796 imperative-statement required; RS09 Format 1 with no WHEN -> COBOL0001; RS14 second WHEN in SEARCH ALL -> COBOL2269. Class c: RS07 EQUALS (not a 1985 relational word) -> COBOL5506; RS15 NOT AT END (not in either 1985 format) -> COBOL0001. Accept half: RS02B WHEN K1 (IX) = 1 + 2 (arithmetic-expression-1) prints 'HIT 03' and WHEN K-THREE (IX) (condition-name-1 alone) prints 'C 03'; RS10B AND condition-name chain prints H; RS11 Format 1 WHEN ... NEXT SENTENCE without END-SEARCH prints 'AFTER 03'; RS12 Format 2 AT END before WHEN, key absent, prints E; RS13 CONTINUE bodies compile and run. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.22.2 'SEARCH ALL identifier-1 [AT END imperative-statement-1]'; OK §1985:VI.6.22.3 SR3 'condition-1 may be any conditional expression'; OK §1985:VI.6.22.3 SR4 'must be subscripted by the first index-name'; OK §1985:VI.6.22.3 SR5 'the NEXT SENTENCE phrase must not be specified'. Weak diagnoses (generic COBOL0001 on misplaced AT END, NOT AT END, missing WHEN) do not change the verdict: each is a compile-time refusal.
